reasons: The cited termination provisions (p0118, p0128–p0131) address only return of Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes and conversion of the license on Garman default; nothing obliges Garman to provide transition assistance, return Sparkling's data, or certify deletion, and the survival list in p0131 contains no exit-assistance provision — so 'missing' is the correct status.

The rule is engaged: the Agreement contemplates Garman handling Sparkling's data (Section 4 inbound data conversion) and services fees, so a data-return/exit mechanic is expected and its absence is not merely a definitional gap.

The inserted new Section 17(d) tracks the model language closely (6 months' transition assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return in commonly used machine-readable format, deletion plus written certification) and is placed in the termination section, so it is an actionable, correctly directed insert with no collateral edits to existing text.

The comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the required prefix, states what changed and why, and offers the 90-day fallback without lecturing; deterministic checks confirm the transition/data-return language is present.
